functional_requirements.raw_text: The Space Fractions system will have an introductory movie to set up the storyline. The movie begins automatically upon entry. The system listens for a mouse click to skip the movie; if clicked, it transitions to the main menu. If not clicked, it plays to completion and then transitions to the main menu.
The system will have a main menu including a brief help section, a summary of the team, a link to the website, and a button to start the game. It also includes a link to the Denominators' web page.

The system will present a series of multiple-choice fraction questions (testing arithmetic, equivalence, graphical interpretation, and improper/proper fractions) that sequentially form a storyline. A friendly robotic sidekick provides hints and usability assistance.

The system must process player inputs for spaceship velocity adjustments based on fraction inputs. Inputs are two integers (numerator, denominator). The system validates integrity (integers, denominator != 0). If valid, it converts the fraction to a decimal and applies it to the spaceship's current velocity. If invalid, it displays an error message and requests new input.

The system must provide immediate feedback for answers. Correct answers display a confirmation message and transition to the next question. Incorrect answers inform the player of the mistake and allow a retry without points. The output is sounds and animations via Flash movies.

The system must implement dynamic and adaptive gameplay where the storyline diverges based on the user's performance at 'critical points' (pivotal questions). The ending scene is determined by these critical decisions.
The ending scene must calculate and display the user's total score with a customized message. It must offer options to quit the system or try again (return to main menu).

A web-accessible Question Updater component must allow administrators to update fraction questions. It requires password authentication. It uses an intuitive web forms interface (pulldown menus, text fields) to edit questions. Data is validated for completeness and relevance before saving.
Updated question data must be saved in a file on the web server in a format that the system sequence can dynamically read and incorporate into gameplay without system restarts.

The Math Umbrella component must provide a menu of links to external S2S projects related to fractions, decimals, and percents. Selecting a link opens the external project in a separate window while keeping the main system active.

non_functional_requirements.raw_text: The system will be as secure as the web browser that will run the product.
Reliability will be ensured by extensive testing by the team members and mentors, if available.
Maintainability is a primary goal for this project.

The interface and information must be effective so that Bobby (competitive user) easily recognizes how to start, and Alice (reluctant user) has no problems navigating the help section. Claire (teacher) is assured students know what to do.

asrs.raw_text: The output of the velocity calculation process is immediate, ensuring responsive gameplay.
The introductory and main menu movies can be downloaded in approximately one minute with a modem connection. The main system can be played within a few minutes with a regular modem connection.
The system will reside on the Internet so more than one user can access the product and download its content for use on their computer. Only one person can use a single instance.

technical_constraints.raw_text: The Space Fractions system requires a web browser capable of running Flash movies.
The Space Fractions system will not be dependent on any other software and is not a component of another program.
The Space Fractions system does not require any new hardware.
